source: Royal Government of Cambodia, General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), "ខែ្សសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំពោតនៅកម្ពុជា" (Corn Production Value Chain in Cambodia), 2017
text:
Among 250 surveyed red-corn farming households, the reasons given for choosing a particular seed variety were, in order of frequency: familiarity/trust in a known seed family or brand (76 households, 30%); high expected yield (54, 22%); it is a popular/trending variety that other farmers in the area are also planting (31, 12%); firm/hard kernel texture (23, 9%); small kernel size (17, 7%); good cob/ear shape (10, 4%); straight rows of kernels on the cob (10, 4%); and early maturity allowing an earlier harvest (2, 1%).

The survey also found that reliability of seed germination is a major farmer concern: seed cost is a small share of total production cost, but poor germination forces costly re-planting and delays the whole season.
